study_identification_part.si4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize the multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus (FFG) by integrating data from structural MRI, resting-state fMRI, task-fMRI, and EEG. The study aimed to identify how individual-level deviations in these modalities, assessed via normative modeling and linked independent component analysis, differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals and relate to social functioning.

rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Here we leveraged a large multimodal sample to study the cross-modal signature of face processing within the FFG across four imaging modalities (structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, task-functional magnetic resonance imaging and electroencephalography) in 204 autistic and nonautistic individuals aged 7-30 years (case-control design).

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: All analyses were restricted to the right and left FFG on the basis of the HOA (Oxford Center for Functional MRI of the Brain) adjusted to have 100% coverage across all individuals for each imaging modality (Supplementary Methods).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: sMRI: CAT12 (SPM12) with DARTEL, 4mm FWHM smoothing; rs-fMRI: FSL v5.0.6 with ICA-AROMA, 6mm FWHM smoothing; task-fMRI: SPM12, 8mm FWHM smoothing; EEG: EEGLab and Fieldtrip (Matlab).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The supplementary methods provide detailed descriptions of the preprocessing pipelines for each modality, including software packages and key steps like smoothing.

Resting-state fMRI data preprocessing...included tools from the FMRIB Software Library (FSL version 5.0.6...)...applying ICA-AROMA...spatial smoothing with a 6mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. fMRI data analysis followed standard processing routines in SPM12...smoothing with an 8mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. Preprocessing and harmonisation of this data was performed at Birkbeck, University of London. rci8_quality_checking.detail: Extensive QC was performed for each modality. sMRI: Exclusions for excessive motion (N=37), atypicalities (N=21), and failed preprocessing (N=3) based on CAT12 reports. rs-fMRI: Exclusions for low volume count, excessive motion (meanFD >0.7mm or maxFD >7.6mm), low coverage, and extreme values. task-fMRI: Exclusions for excessive motion (>20% trials with meanFD > 0.5mm; N=47). EEG: Exclusions for technical errors, incomplete battery, too few trials (<20), or too few channels (<75%). Motion/QC parameters (FD, D-VARS) did not differ between final groups.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Structural T1-weighted images with excessive head motion (N=37)...were excluded. Resting-state fMRI...Scans with...excessive head motion...were excluded. Hariri task-fMRI datasets with excessive head motion...were excluded. EEG data...Images with technical/upload errors..., incomplete EEG battery..., too few trials..., and too few channels...were excluded.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Site effects were handled by including 'scanning site' as a covariate in the Bayesian linear regression normative models for each imaging modality. The study also explicitly tested for and found no significant effects of site or diagnosis-by-site interactions on the primary group-differentiating component (IC44).

nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: Here, we trained normative models using Bayesian linear regression 98 for each brain imaging modality within the right and left FFG region of interest (ROI) independently using age, sex and scanning site as covariates.

nm4_response_variable.answer: The response variables were imaging-derived features from the fusiform gyrus (FFG) for four modalities: 1) Voxel-wise gray matter (GM) volumes from VBM. 2) Voxel-wise seed-based connectivity (Fisher's z-transformed correlation) between the individual's FFA peak and all other FFG voxels for rs-fMRI. 3) Voxel-wise T-contrast maps (faces vs. shapes) for task-fMRI. 4) The first principal component of source-reconstructed time series across 18 cortical parcels within the FFG for EEG.
nm4_response_variable.reason: The methods section clearly lists the specific imaging-derived feature used as the response variable for each of the four modalities.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: In summary, the features for subsequent normative modeling were as follows (1) structure: voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-derived, voxel-wise GM volumes, (2) rs-fMRI: seed-based correlation between the FFA and the remaining FFG, (3) task-fMRI: T-contrast maps reflecting sensitivity to faces and (4) EEG: the principal component of source-reconstructed activation obtained across different cortical FFG parcels.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: The primary deviation metric was the Z-score, derived from normative probability maps for each individual at each voxel/timepoint. For unimodal group comparisons, extreme deviations were defined using a threshold of |Z| > 2.6. For the primary multimodal analysis, the unthresholded Z-deviation maps from all modalities were merged using Linked Independent Component Analysis (LICA).
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The methods section clearly describes the use of Z-scores as the fundamental deviation metric and explains how these were used in subsequent unimodal (thresholded) and multimodal (unthresholded maps fed into LICA) analyses.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: ...we derived normative probability maps that quantify the deviation from the normative model summarized in Z -scores...To assess whether autistic and NAI differed in their extreme deviations based on unimodal features, thresholded Z -scores ( Z > |2.6|...)...we merged the different individual-level deviations from all imaging modalities (GM volume, FFA connectivity, T-maps...and the principal components of the source-reconstructed time series) using LICA

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group differences in subject loadings from LICA were tested using two-sample t-tests with FDR correction. A support vector machine (SVM) with 10-fold cross-validation was used to test the efficacy of unimodal vs. multimodal components in classifying diagnostic groups. Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) with permutation testing (10,000 iterations) was used to model the multivariate relationship between multimodal independent components (ICs) and two sets of clinical/cognitive features (social-communicative and nonsocial).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Multimodal neural signatures within the fusiform gyrus, derived from normative models, differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals more effectively than unimodal signatures and are specifically associated with social-communicative functioning in autism.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: A multimodal independent component (IC44) showed a significant group difference, with autistic individuals having higher contributions (t=3.5, p_FDR=0.027), driven mainly by rs-fMRI and EEG deviations in face-selective and retinotopic FFG regions. In a classification task, multimodal components significantly outperformed unimodal ones in differentiating autistic from non-autistic individuals (AUC 0.64 vs. 0.48, p<0.001). Furthermore, canonical correlation analysis revealed a significant multivariate association between the set of multimodal components and social-communicative features (r=0.65, p_FDR=0.008), an association not found with nonsocial features. This brain-behavior link was driven by ICs related to atypical structure and function in both higher-order face-selective and lower-order retinotopic areas of the FFG.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study's focus was restricted to a single brain region (FFG), not the whole face-processing network. The sample size for the multimodal analysis (N=204) was significantly reduced from the initial cohort, limiting statistical power. The small number of female, left-handed, and ambidextrous participants prevented stratified analyses for sex and handedness.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: At the same time, it needs to be pointed out that face processing involves an extended neural network across the whole brain...It may thus seem too simplistic to reduce face processing to a single brain region...Here, from a sample of over 600 individuals in the EU-AIMS LEAP dataset, we were able to conduct an analysis in just over 200 individuals who had available imaging data across the four different modalities...in the current study we did not run sex-stratified analyses owing to the small number of female participants...Owing to the small number of left-handed or ambidextrous individuals in our sample, it is not surprising that we did not find an association with handedness.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study combined normative modeling to generate individual-level deviation maps for each modality with Linked Independent Component Analysis (LICA) to achieve data-driven multimodal fusion. This approach allowed for the integration of four different imaging modalities to identify shared patterns of inter-subject variability (multimodal ICs) related to diagnosis and clinical features.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study combines normative modeling with Linked Independent Component Analysis (LICA) to create a multimodal signature of brain differences in autism, focusing specifically on the fusiform gyrus. The final sample of 204 participants represents a subset of the larger EU-AIMS LEAP cohort (>600 individuals) who had complete, usable data across all four imaging modalities (sMRI, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG). The authors note that the term 'normative' refers to a statistical norm (like a growth chart) and is not intended to conflict with the neurodiversity framework. Missing clinical data were handled using imputation.
